body.statement:
Whenever Algorithms 1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser return an identifying functional using only selector values in \(H\) and divisions by margins supported on \(\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^{+})\), that derivation has a finite support-licensed translation into the selector-correction, reachable-fixing, and labelled-elimination primitives of \(\operatorname{SA\mbox{-}CS\mbox{-}ID}\). Its composite is a rational circuit \(F_H\) with a denominator registry \(\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}}\) and domain \(\mathfrak D_H\) such that
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H,\qquad
 F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta)\quad\text{for every }\theta\in\Theta_H.
\]
After gate reinsertion, the translated circuit and all of its required positive margins are algebraically equal to the published derivation on the original expansion. This assertion establishes preservation of the published formula; it does not assert that the presently specified deterministic priority schedule selects the translating trace.
body.justification: Completeness is useful only if it retains the positive formulas already justified by the anchor algorithm.
body.gap: Tabell, Tikka, and Karvanen transport do-calculus formulas through ordinary pruning and clustering, but not through fixed-support selector-image normalization.
body.consumer: Existing systematic-selection analyses obtain the same estimand and can adopt the normalized backend without changing valid reported formulas.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a successful published derivation satisfying the two hypotheses in the statement. At every context \(s\) used by that derivation, \(s\in H\). Its initial conditional table is
\[
 q_s(v)
 =p_H(V=v\mid S=s)
 =\frac{p_H(v,s)}
 {\sum_{v':(v',s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)}p_H(v',s)}.
\tag{1}
\]
The denominator in (1) is a nonempty sum: exact selector support gives \(p_\theta(S=s)>0\), and the summands indexed by structurally admissible cells are strictly positive by \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\). Thus (1) is the context initialization recorded by the selector-correction primitive, and its normalizer is positive.

We translate the finite published derivation inductively. Suppose first that its next operation uses a forced selector value \(x_s\) at a selector-controlled vertex \(X\). By the known zero--one multiplexer stored in the normalized syntax, evaluation at context \(s\) replaces that occurrence by \(\mathbf 1\{X=x_s\}\). Substitution of \(x_s\) into every child is evaluation of the same recursive structural equation. Hence the old and new context kernels agree polynomially subject to the stored gate and coordinate-copy equations. This is exactly the algebraic selector-correction primitive.

Suppose next that the published derivation fixes \(W\) in a reachable district \(D\). Its graphical premise is
\[
 \operatorname{dis}_{D}(W)\cap\operatorname{de}_{D}(W)=\{W\}.
\tag{2}
\]
The translated operation divides the same labelled kernel by the same conditional margin
\[
 m_{s,W}=\sum_{x_W}K_{s,D}.
\tag{3}
\]
Multiplication of the successor kernel by (3) recovers the predecessor kernel, so the required fixing identity follows by cross-multiplication. By the hypothesis on the published derivation, (3) is a supported margin. More generally, every denominator generated after algebraic cancellation has the ledger factorization required by \(\textnormal{def:sa-csid-machine}\). The frozen lemma \(\textnormal{lem:restricted-support-denominator-positivity}\) therefore makes each such division valid at every \(O_H(\theta)\), \(\theta\in\Theta_H\).

For a marginalization step, finite distributivity gives the identical translated circuit
\[
 \sum_Z\prod_{k\in L}K_k.
\tag{4}
\]
For a proper-district step, the normalized topological order gives the same ordered district factors as the published factorization. Cancelling a common factor does not alter the value wherever the uncancelled expression is defined, and every remaining divisor is registered. Equations (1)--(4) therefore prove by induction that each intermediate translated kernel equals its published counterpart.

The derivation tree and every alphabet are finite, so the translated composite is a finite rational circuit \(F_H\). Let \(\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}}\) consist of its reduced context normalizers, fixing margins, and elimination denominators, and let \(\mathfrak D_H\) be the domain from \(\textnormal{def:circuit-domain}\). The restricted-support positivity lemma gives
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H.
\tag{5}
\]
The premise says that the terminal published functional identifies the target. The inductive circuit equality and \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\), which identifies normalized evaluation with evaluation after restoring the original gates, now yield
\[
 F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta)
 \qquad(\theta\in\Theta_H).
\tag{6}
\]
Every context used in the construction was one of the published contexts and hence belonged to \(H\). This proves the narrowed preservation statement.
